title: Red Herring — Harmless Deploy Coincides with DB Slowdown
description: order-service:v1.8.3 (a cosmetic text change) is deployed at the exact same time a DB slowdown begins (simulated lock contention from a batch job). The deploy is innocent: latency is caused entirely by db_slow. The correlated deploy event is the trap.

true_root_cause.summary: db_slow=true with db_slow_seconds=2.0 (batch-job lock contention) — every DB query takes ≥2 s; the coincident v1.8.3 deploy is cosmetic and unrelated

key_evidence_signals.expected_behaviour: p95 jumps to ≥2 s for every operation right after the deploy timestamp
p95 rises to ≥2 s across all endpoints (GET and POST)
Ratio UNCHANGED — v1.8.3 did not alter the query pattern, proving the deploy is not an N+1 regression
Remains near zero — a bad deploy would typically change behaviour; here only latency moved
Row order-service@v1.8.3 exists at the incident start timestamp — correlation bait, NOT causation

red_herrings: Deploy event at the same timestamp as the failure — correlation is not causation
v1.8.3 notes say 'text change in /health response' — cosmetic, cannot affect latency
Rolling back to v1.8.1 would NOT fix the latency, because the DB layer is the problem
recommended_fix: Do NOT roll back — resolve the DB slowness (batch-job lock contention / missing index). The deploy is innocent; verify by checking that the query-count ratio is unchanged
evaluation_checks: Agent identifies db_slow as the true root cause, NOT the v1.8.3 deploy
Agent cites db_query_duration_seconds p95 ≥ 2 s as primary evidence
Agent confirms the query-count ratio is stable (v1.8.3 did not change query behaviour)
Agent does NOT recommend rolling back as the primary fix
